Purpose and exclusions

Single authenticated service for character identity, persistence, economic transactions, zone allocation and social endpoints; PostgreSQL18 durability.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Install pinned .NET10 SDK and PostgreSQL18 locally; choose a supported provider version after compatibility check. No backend binary or runnable service is supplied.
  2. Create one solution/app and configure development secrets outside repository. Apply base schema migration and run identity/command fixture tests before connecting UE.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Functions, commands and event bindings

Project custom contracts are not engine/plugin nodes. A read-only asset participates through its consumer; it does not inherit that consumer’s mutation methods. Backend endpoint pages label transport proposals explicitly.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Character persistence, schema, command receipts and sessions. Rule owner: URPGCharacterServiceAdapter. This asset’s role is Single authenticated service for character identity, persistence, economic transactions, zone allocation and social endpoints; PostgreSQL18 durability.

  1. Zone adapter authenticates as a trusted server and includes CharacterId, zone ID, fencing epoch, expected revision, command ID and bounded validated payload.
  2. Backend validates the server capability and current lease; it never trusts a client to select a privileged operation or pass a completed gameplay event.
  3. Open a short database transaction; look up or insert the unique command record and compare request hash. A reused ID with different data rejects.
  4. Lock all affected ownership/economy/source rows in a consistent order, revalidate constraints, apply all changes, increment revision and store result/audit/outbox rows atomically.
  5. Commit before returning success. Zone applies the returned snapshot/delta on the game thread only if its session epoch and request generation still match.
  6. Timeout means outcome unknown: suspend conflicting writes, query receipt or retry the identical command. A committed result is returned without consuming/granting again.
  7. On restart, revoke expired leases, migrate supported records, and restore accepted facts; no widget or local SaveGame can override the snapshot.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: ServiceFixture_CharacterStore / Account_A / Character_A / L_NetworkLab. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Lost response after commit -> GetCommandReceipt returns one original result; no second grant.
Same command ID/different payload -> IdempotencyConflict; original receipt remains unchanged.
Old source server uses epoch N after transfer to N+1 -> SessionFenced; no write.
Concurrent withdraw/craft using same item -> consistent lock/revision policy accepts only a valid serial outcome.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
